        Idea:
Build a holistic VibeComfy template porting workbench/toolset, based on the failures seen while porting production Reigh workflows to VibeComfy. The toolset should make it easy to find/import source Comfy workflows, convert them into proper Python ready-template/scratchpad format, preserve provenance, infer and validate custom node packs, infer and HEAD-check model asset URLs, resolve UI-only/helper nodes like Note/MarkdownNote/SetNode/GetNode and similar reroute/broadcast helpers, detect positional widget aliases by comparing compiled API prompts with Comfy object_info/schema, surface missing required inputs before a RunPod burn, emit actionable reports and tests, and support battle-testing against both a simple template and the current WanAnimate production-parity template. It should be pragmatic: build the first useful slice now, use it immediately on the current failures, and document the remaining roadmap. Avoid raw JSON execution as the steady-state path; workflows should land as Python-esque VibeComfy ready templates/scratchpads. Include a strategy for integrating this into the live validation loop so future users avoid the same URL/model/custom-node/schema failures.

User notes and answers:
- User added: discoverability is a first-class requirement. The VibeComfy porting toolset must make it obvious to humans and agents when to use it: command names/help, README/authoring docs, AGENTS.md or skill guidance, and failure/live-validation docs should all point to port check before manual template editing or expensive RunPod validation. The tool should document when to use check, convert, doctor/validate, model URL checks, custom-node pack discovery, and Python-template conversion.

        Idea:
Build a holistic VibeComfy template porting workbench/toolset, based on the failures seen while porting production Reigh workflows to VibeComfy. The toolset should make it easy to find/import source Comfy workflows, convert them into proper Python ready-template/scratchpad format, preserve provenance, infer and validate custom node packs, infer and HEAD-check model asset URLs, resolve UI-only/helper nodes like Note/MarkdownNote/SetNode/GetNode and similar reroute/broadcast helpers, detect positional widget aliases by comparing compiled API prompts with Comfy object_info/schema, surface missing required inputs before a RunPod burn, emit actionable reports and tests, and support battle-testing against both a simple template and the current WanAnimate production-parity template. It should be pragmatic: build the first useful slice now, use it immediately on the current failures, and document the remaining roadmap. Avoid raw JSON execution as the steady-state path; workflows should land as Python-esque VibeComfy ready templates/scratchpads. Include a strategy for integrating this into the live validation loop so future users avoid the same URL/model/custom-node/schema failures.

User notes and answers:
- User added: discoverability is a first-class requirement. The VibeComfy porting toolset must make it obvious to humans and agents when to use it: command names/help, README/authoring docs, AGENTS.md or skill guidance, and failure/live-validation docs should all point to port check before manual template editing or expensive RunPod validation. The tool should document when to use check, convert, doctor/validate, model URL checks, custom-node pack discovery, and Python-template conversion.

url=url_value,\n+        subdir=subdir,\n+        source=source,\n+        node_id=node_id,\n+        class_type=class_type or None,\n+        metadata=metadata,\n+    )\n+\n+\n+def tuple[int, str]:\n+    try:\n+        return (int(node_id), str(node_id))\n+    except (TypeError, ValueError):\n+        return (10**12, str(node_id))\n+\n+\n+__all__ = [\n+    \"AssetAnalysis\",\n+         Idea:
Build a holistic VibeComfy template porting workbench/toolset, based on the failures seen while porting production Reigh workflows to VibeComfy. The toolset should make it easy to find/import source Comfy workflows, convert them into proper Python ready-template/scratchpad format, preserve provenance, infer and validate custom node packs, infer and HEAD-check model asset URLs, resolve UI-only/helper nodes like Note/MarkdownNote/SetNode/GetNode and similar reroute/broadcast helpers, detect positional widget aliases by comparing compiled API prompts with Comfy object_info/schema, surface missing required inputs before a RunPod burn, emit actionable reports and tests, and support battle-testing against both a simple template and the current WanAnimate production-parity template. It should be pragmatic: build the first useful slice now, use it immediately on the current failures, and document the remaining roadmap. Avoid raw JSON execution as the steady-state path; workflows should land as Python-esque VibeComfy ready templates/scratchpads. Include a strategy for integrating this into the live validation loop so future users avoid the same URL/model/custom-node/schema failures.

User notes and answers:
- User added: discoverability is a first-class requirement. The VibeComfy porting toolset must make it obvious to humans and agents when to use it: command names/help, README/authoring docs, AGENTS.md or skill guidance, and failure/live-validation docs should all point to port check before manual template editing or expensive RunPod validation. The tool should document when to use check, convert, doctor/validate, model URL checks, custom-node pack discovery, and Python-template conversion.

        Idea:
Build a holistic VibeComfy template porting workbench/toolset, based on the failures seen while porting production Reigh workflows to VibeComfy. The toolset should make it easy to find/import source Comfy workflows, convert them into proper Python ready-template/scratchpad format, preserve provenance, infer and validate custom node packs, infer and HEAD-check model asset URLs, resolve UI-only/helper nodes like Note/MarkdownNote/SetNode/GetNode and similar reroute/broadcast helpers, detect positional widget aliases by comparing compiled API prompts with Comfy object_info/schema, surface missing required inputs before a RunPod burn, emit actionable reports and tests, and support battle-testing against both a simple template and the current WanAnimate production-parity template. It should be pragmatic: build the first useful slice now, use it immediately on the current failures, and document the remaining roadmap. Avoid raw JSON execution as the steady-state path; workflows should land as Python-esque VibeComfy ready templates/scratchpads. Include a strategy for integrating this into the live validation loop so future users avoid the same URL/model/custom-node/schema failures.

User notes and answers:
- User added: discoverability is a first-class requirement. The VibeComfy porting toolset must make it obvious to humans and agents when to use it: command names/help, README/authoring docs, AGENTS.md or skill guidance, and failure/live-validation docs should all point to port check before manual template editing or expensive RunPod validation. The tool should document when to use check, convert, doctor/validate, model URL checks, custom-node pack discovery, and Python-template conversion.

  "patch": "*** Begin Patch\n*** Add File: docs/template_porting_workbench.md\n+# Template Porting Workbench\n+\n+The porting workbench is the first stop when importing or repairing a ComfyUI workflow for VibeComfy. Run it before hand-editing a converted template, before spending RunPod time, and whenever a raw workflow fails with missing custom nodes, schema errors, model asset problems, helper nodes, or positional `widget_N` ambiguity.\n+\n+The steady-state output should be Python: an editable scratchpad or a ready-template candidate. Raw JSON is source material, not the long-term authoring surface.\n+\n+## Quick Start\n+\n+```bash\n+python -m vibecomfy.cli port check <workflow> --json\n+python -m vibecomfy.cli port convert <workflow> --out out/scratchpads/<id>.py --json\n+python -m vibecomfy.cli port convert <workflow> --ready-id <kind>/<name> --out ready_templates/<kind>/<name>.py --json\n+```\n+\n+Use `<workflow>` as a ready id, scratchpad path, raw JSON path, or indexed workflow reference. `port check` is offline by default and cheap enough to run before every manual template edit and before every RunPod validation attempt.\n+\n+## When To Use Each Command\n+\n+| Need | Command |\n+| --- | --- |\n+| Preflight a source workflow before editing or RunPod | `python -m vibecomfy.cli port check <workflow> --json` |\n+| Turn raw JSON or an indexed workflow into editable Python | `python -m vibecomfy.cli port convert <workflow> --out out/scratchpads/<id>.py --json` |\n+| Produce a ready-template candidate | `python -m vibecomfy.cli port convert <workflow> --ready-id <kind>/<name> --out ready_templates/<kind>/<name>.py --json` |\n+| Validate an authored scratchpad or ready template | `python -m vibecomfy.cli validate <scratchpad-or-template.py>` |\n+| Diagnose runtime readiness and suggested fixes | `python -m vibecomfy.cli doctor <workflow>` |\n+| See custom-node packs to install | `python -m vibecomfy.cli nodes install-plan <workflow>` |\n+| Fetch declared model assets | `python -m vibecomfy.cli fetch <workflow>` |\n+| Check model URLs without downloading bodies | `python -m vibecomfy.cli port check <workflow> --head-check-models --json` |\n+\n+`--head-check-models` is opt-in. It performs HEAD requests only, follows redirects, records status codes, and does not download model bodies. Keep normal `run`, `doctor`, `validate`, and `fetch` behavior offline unless you intentionally ask for URL checks.\n+\n+## What `port check` Reports\n+\n+The report is a stable JSON object with provenance, source hash, workflow shape, node counts, diagnostics, custom-node pack suggestions, model asset candidates, optional URL check results, artifacts, and recommendations.\n+\n+It catches the failure classes that previously surfaced only after conversion or on a GPU:\n+\n+- helper and UI-only nodes such as `Note`, `MarkdownNote`, `SetNode`, and `GetNode`;\n+- unresolved helper broadcasts before compile can silently drop them;\n+- missing real runtime class types and matching node-pack suggestions;\n+- unknown classes, missing required inputs, invalid link shapes, and schema type mismatches;\n+- filename-only or missing model asset URLs;\n+- duplicate model URL targets and opt-in HEAD failures such as 404 or license-gated responses;\n+- unresolved positional `widget_N` aliases using widget-only schemas so link-only sockets do not shift widget positions.\n+\n+Helper/UI classes are never treated as installable missing packs. They produce helper diagnostics. Real unresolved runtime classes remain hard porting errors.\n+\n+## Convert Modes\n+\n+Scratchpad mode is the default and is the right choice while investigating a workflow:\n+\n+```bash\n+python -m vibecomfy.cli port convert workflow_corpus/community/example.json \\\n+  --out out/scratchpads/example.py \\\n+  --json\n+```\n+\n+Ready-template mode is explicit because it creates a curated candidate with template identity:\n+\n+```bash\n+python -m vibecomfy.cli port convert workflow_corpus/community/example.json \\\n+  --ready-id image/example \\\n+  --out ready_templates/image/example.py \\\n+  --json\n+```\n+\n+The converter validates emitted Python by importing the module, calling `build()`, compiling API output, and running schema validation when a provider is available.\n+\n+## Live Validation Loop\n+\n+Run this order while porting:\n+\n+1. `port check <workflow> --json`\n+2. `nodes install-plan <workflow>` when unresolved runtime classes appear\n+3. `fetch <workflow>` when declared models are missing\n+4. `port convert <workflow> --out out/scratchpads/<id>.py --json`\n+5. `validate out/scratchpads/<id>.py`\n+6. `doctor out/scratchpads/<id>.py`\n+7. focused RunPod validation only after the local report has no hard porting errors\n+\n+The RunPod corpus matrix writes an offline port report and a port-convert preview next to existing logs so GPU failures can be traced back to cheap local preflight results. Those reports are advisory artifacts; they do not make network checks mandatory.\n+\n+## Battle Targets\n+\n+Use a small source workflow first to verify the path quickly, then run the current production-parity target:\n+\n+```bash\n+python -m vibecomfy.cli port check image/z_image --json\n+python -m vibecomfy.cli port check video/wanvideo_wrapper_22_wan_animate_preprocess_kijai --json\n+```\n+\n+Add `--head-check-models` only when you specifically need URL reachability diagnostics.\n+\n+## Roadmap\n+\n+The first useful slice is intentionally pragmatic: source loading, helper stripping, custom-node pack inference, model asset analysis, opt-in URL HEAD checks, widget alias diagnostics, Python emission, CLI preflights, doctor guidance, and RunPod report artifacts.\n+\n+Remaining work belongs in later batches:\n+\n+- broaden CLI and parity tests across simple and WanAnimate paths;\n+- expand docs and agent guidance as new failure modes land;\n+- keep improving schema/object-info coverage for custom nodes;\n+- promote recurring RunPod failures into deterministic local checks where possible.\n*** End Patch\n"
}

Inspect those before debugging pod-only symptoms; they often identify missing packs, model declarations, helper-node problems, or schema issues without another GPU run.\n@@\n | \"New full graph for a new model\" | Add a ready workflow under `ready_templates/<kind>/...` (see \"Adding a new workflow\") |\n | \"Run on a GPU I don't have locally\" | `scripts/runpod_validate.py` or the `--runpod` pytest markers |\n-| \"Inspect why something doesn't run\" | `inspect`, `doctor`, `analyze info/trace/path/values`, then `validate` |\n+| \"Inspect why an imported or converted workflow doesn't run\" | `port check <workflow> --json`, then `nodes install-plan`, `fetch`, `validate`, or `doctor` based on the report |\n+| \"Inspect why authored Python doesn't run\" | `inspect`, `doctor`, `analyze info/trace/path/values`, then `validate` |\n@@\n 2. **Drop the source JSON** under `workflow_corpus/official/<media>/<id>.json`, `workflow_corpus/custom_nodes/<pack>/<source>/<id>.json`, or `workflow_corpus/community/<source>/<id>.json`. Keep it close to upstream.\n-3. **Declare custom nodes** in `vibecomfy/node_packs.py` (a `CustomNodePack(name, repo, classes, pip_packages)` entry) and pin in `custom_nodes.lock`.\n-4. **Declare models**: workflow-embedded URLs go in workflow metadata; node-pack-specific layouts go in `vibecomfy/registry/models.yaml`.\n-5. **Add a manifest row** in `workflow_corpus/manifests/coverage.json` with `id`, `path`, `media`, `task`, `coverage_tier`, `ready_template: true`.\n-6. **Optional materializer policy** in `scripts/materialize_ready_templates.py` if the source needs smoke-time normalization (lower res / steps, fixture injection, deterministic seeds).\n-7. **Generate** the ready Python file with `uv run python scripts/materialize_ready_templates.py` (or hand-author it under `ready_templates/<media>/<id>.py` for full control — see `ready_templates/image/z_image.py` for the canonical hand-authored shape).\n-8. **Validate locally**: `vibecomfy validate ready_templates/<media>/<id>.py`, then targeted tests `pytest -q tests/test_ready_templates.py tests/test_runpod_matrix.py tests/test_nodes_install.py tests/test_cli.py`.\n-9. **Validate on RunPod** with a focused scope: `VIBECOMFY_MATRIX_SCOPE=<family> uv run python scripts/runpod_corpus_matrix.py`. Don't run the full matrix while iterating.\n-10. **Document failures** in `docs/hiddenswitch_incompatibilities.md`, `docs/structural_issues.md`, or a family coverage doc — never leave fixes only in chat history or pod logs.\n+3. **Run port preflight**: `python -m vibecomfy.cli port check workflow_corpus/.../<id>.json --json`. Resolve hard errors before hand-editing or RunPod.\n+4. **Declare custom nodes** in `vibecomfy/node_packs.py` (a `CustomNodePack(name, repo, classes, pip_packages)` entry) and pin in `custom_nodes.lock`.\n+5. **Declare models**: workflow-embedded URLs go in workflow metadata; node-pack-specific layouts go in `vibecomfy/registry/models.yaml`.\n+6. **Convert to Python** with `python -m vibecomfy.cli port convert workflow_corpus/.../<id>.json --out out/scratchpads/<id>.py --json`; use `--ready-id <kind>/<name>` only for ready-template candidates.\n+7. **Add a manifest row** in `workflow_corpus/manifests/coverage.json` with `id`, `path`, `media`, `task`, `coverage_tier`, `ready_template: true`.\n+8. **Optional materializer policy** in `scripts/materialize_ready_templates.py` if the source needs smoke-time normalization (lower res / steps, fixture injection, deterministic seeds).\n+9. **Generate** the ready Python file with `uv run python scripts/materialize_ready_templates.py` (or hand-author it under `ready_templates/<media>/<id>.py` for full control — see `ready_templates/image/z_image.py` for the canonical hand-authored shape).\n+10. **Validate locally**: `vibecomfy validate ready_templates/<media>/<id>.py`, then targeted tests `pytest -q tests/test_ready_templates.py tests/test_runpod_matrix.py tests/test_nodes_install.py tests/test_cli.py`.\n+11. **Validate on RunPod** with a focused scope: `VIBECOMFY_MATRIX_SCOPE=<family> uv run python scripts/runpod_corpus_matrix.py`. Don't run the full matrix while iterating.\n+12. **Document failures** in `docs/hiddenswitch_incompatibilities.md`, `docs/structural_issues.md`, or a family coverage doc — never leave fixes only in chat history or pod logs.\n@@\n - `docs/authoring.md` — blocks, patches, handles, opaque subgraphs, recipes, escape hatches\n+- `docs/template_porting_workbench.md` — `port check`, `port convert`, model URL checks, custom-node pack discovery, and RunPod preflight loop\n - `docs/vibeworkflow.md` — IR contract\n*** End Patch\n"

It should be pragmatic: build the first useful slice now, use it immediately on the current failures, and document the remaining roadmap. Avoid raw JSON execution as the steady-state path; workflows should land as Python-esque VibeComfy ready templates/scratchpads. Include a strategy for integrating this into the live validation loop so future users avoid the same URL/model/custom-node/schema failures.
